title: Chicken Tikka Masala
shortDescription: Rich curry on a busy night
subtitle: Rich curry on a busy night
description: Rich curry on a busy night. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep components
steps.instruction: Dice vegetables; measure sauce ingredients. Chicken Tikka Masala moves smoother when everything is on the counter before the burner goes on.

steps.title: Sear and finish
steps.instruction: Sear protein over medium-high until browned, then finish in sauce or oven until safe temp (165°F poultry, 160°F ground beef). Watch for color and spring-back, not clock alone.

steps.title: Reduce and season
steps.instruction: Simmer sauce until it coats a spoon. Taste for salt and acid — add a splash of vinegar or lemon if flat.

steps.title: Plate for the hall
steps.instruction: Serve on sheet trays for family-style or portioned plates. Hold backup at 200°F; cover lightly with foil so skins stay crisp where applicable.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Tikka Masala with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chicken Tikka Masala on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Rich curry on a busy night. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
